verses.translation: Only by the grace of God does the desire for non-duality arise in the wise, which delivers them from the great fear of worldly existence.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं ते निर्गुणे तत्त्वे कल्पयिष्यामि वा गुणान् ।
आत्मानं सततं शान्तं निर्विकल्पं निरामयम् ॥
verses.translation: How shall I attribute qualities to that Reality which is beyond all qualities? The Self is ever peaceful, free of all distinctions and ailments.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मैव केवलं सत्यं सर्वं ब्रह्ममयं जगत् ।
न मृत्युर्न च मे जन्म न बन्धो न च मे गतिः ॥
verses.translation: The Self alone is the sole truth; the entire universe is pervaded by Brahman. There is no death for me, no birth, no bondage, no journey.

verses.sanskrit:
पवनवदनिर्देशो विश्वमात्रेति यः स्थितः ।
स एव स्वयमात्मानमात्मनैवावलोकयेत् ॥
verses.translation: Like the wind which is imperceptible, the Self pervades as the entire cosmos. One should see the Self by the Self alone.

verses.sanskrit:
नाहं देहो न मे देहो बोधोऽहम् इति निश्चिनु ।
एवं विचारयन् विद्वान् आत्मारामो विरजस्कः ॥
verses.translation: I am not the body, nor is the body mine — I am pure consciousness. Determine this with certainty. Thus reflecting, the wise one rejoices in the Self, free from impurity.
